why: Wired Head is the Tyger Claws' braindance club on Crescent and Broad in Japantown: a ground-floor bar and BD lounge with couches, vending machines and a tablet counter, and a mezzanine rail above, used in vanilla as the gang's hideout. In the Greed Never Pays gig it holds Leah Gladen's body, her stolen CorpCracker and the Tyger Claws who fight V for it. This proposal restores the club as a working venue in the no-gig timeline: the quest interior section plus its ten Tyger Claws, relaxing at the bar, couches, vending machine and balcony rail with their netrunner at a tablet. No corpse, no firefight and no named quest cast are restored.

open_questions: Walk in from Crescent and Broad and confirm the club is open for business through the glass double doors, with no gig marker and no locked entrance.

Count the crowd inside: about ten Tyger Claws should be sitting and standing at the bar couches, the vending machine, the tablet counter and the balcony rail, all relaxed, with the netrunner at a tablet.
Look up at the mezzanine: the ganger on the rail should be standing on the upper level (about 30 m up), not floating or clipped into the balcony.
Check the back room behind the shutter: no body, no shard and no CorpCracker should be visible or reachable there, and the shutter may stay vanilla.
Check the wall TVs in the bar: they should be powered and interactive, since the q003 phases that disable their interaction never run.

communities.why: The whole community is Wired Head's standing Tyger Claw crew: one officer, eight gunmen and a rare netrunner, all in initial phase A on relaxed workspots (bar couch, drink can, vending machine, tablet, BD couch, balcony rail). Vanilla switches the same whole community on as the bar's occupants when the fight starts; restoring it whole in the same phase gives the club its staff, security and patrons without any combat.

proximity_wait.why: The glass double entrance door on the normal way into the club, resolved to its full $/ path in input.json devices and driven by the venue's openworld phase (ForcePower, then ForceClose/ForceUnpower). A device, not a workspot, so the proximity wait fires.
